newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-LENTINI HOPES SOUNESS WILL HELP TORINO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LENTINI HOPES SOUNESS WILL HELP TORINO.

text.p: Gianluigi Lentini, once the world's most expensive soccer player, hopes his return to lowly Torino next season after five years in serie A would pay off with promotion under new manager Graeme Souness.
"I've just met Souness. I don't know how he's going to make Torino play. All I know is he has to take us back into serie A," Lentini told Friday's Gazzetta dello Sport.
The 28-year-old striker said he decided to give up serie A soccer because he felt Torino, the club where he played before moving to Milan in 1992 for a reported $14 million, could become great again.
"The side is serious. They are building a side able to go up into serie A and stay there. Honestly, I would have never played in Serie B. I made an exception just for Torino," Lentini said.
"I left (Torino) because of money. It was too hard to say no. I was young, Milan's offer was too good to refuse. Now I've made money, I can take other things into consideration."
Torino, relegated from serie A after the 1995-96 season, started their promotion drive earlier this month by hiring former player Souness from Southampton on a reported two-year contract.
Lentini, who met the former Scottish international at Torino's last match in June, played the 1996-7 season at serie A side Atalanta on loan from Milan.
After moving from Torino, he spent most of his time on the bench at Milan after a motorway accident in 1993 on the way back from a friendly in Genoa that left him in a coma for 24 hours.
Lentini never regained his first team place, playing only 26 out of 68 league games. He also has 13 international caps, the latest against Bosnia in Sarajevo last year.
